record.paper_title: Analysis on Faddeev Knots and Skyrme Solitons: Recent Progress and Open Problems
record.original_question: In the classical three-dimensional Skyrme model, finite-energy static fields define maps from R^3 ∪ {∞} ≅ S^3 to S^3, so each field has an integer topological degree N in π3(S^3). For every integer degree N, does there exist a finite-energy static field that minimizes the Skyrme energy among all configurations with degree N?

evidence.quote: In the classical Skyrme model, the field configurations are topologically represented by the homotopy group π3(S3) and the fundamental mathematical question is to ask whether there is a static Skyrme energy minimizer among each homotopy class.

which is the topological degree of φ when viewed as a map from S3 = R3 ∪ {∞} into itself. The topological solitons in the Skyrme model are then the solutions of the constrained minimization problem (3.13) EN = inf{E(φ) | E(φ) < ∞, Q(φ) = N}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the classical three-dimensional Skyrme model. A static field is a map φ : ℝ³ → S³ ⊂ ℝ⁴ with φ(x) → φ_∞ as |x| → ∞ for some fixed point φ_∞ ∈ S³, so that φ extends continuously to a map from the one-point compactification S³ ≅ ℝ³ ∪ {∞} into S³. The Skyrme energy is

  E(φ) = ∫_{ℝ³} ( (1/2) Σ_{i=1}^{3} |∂_i φ|² + (1/4) Σ_{1 ≤ i < j ≤ 3} |∂_i φ ∧ ∂_j φ|² ) dx,

where ∂_i φ ∧ ∂_j φ denotes the wedge product of the two ℝ⁴-valued vectors ∂_i φ and ∂_j φ in ⋀² ℝ⁴, with norm taken in ⋀² ℝ⁴. Each finite-energy configuration φ has an integer topological degree

  Q(φ) = deg(φ : S³ → S³) ∈ π₃(S³) ≅ ℤ.

For each integer N ∈ ℤ, set

  E_N = inf { E(φ) : φ : ℝ³ → S³ with E(φ) < ∞ and Q(φ) = N }.

Question: For every integer N, does there exist a finite-energy static map φ_N with Q(φ_N) = N and E(φ_N) = E_N? That is, is the infimum E_N attained for every topological degree N ∈ ℤ?
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of Skyrme energy minimizers in every degree N is a long-standing question. Partial results exist: minimizers are known to be attainable for degree ±1 and, more generally, whenever the energy levels satisfy a strict "substantial inequality" preventing energy splitting (Lin–Yang and related work). However, attainability of E_N for every integer degree N in the classical 3D Skyrme model has not been established in full generality and remains open, since concentration-compactness arguments can fail to rule out splitting into well-separated lower-degree pieces.

status_evidence.title: Energy Splitting, Substantial Inequality, and Minimization for the Faddeev and Skyrme Models
status_evidence.snippet: Lin–Yang substantial inequality is used to recover compactness and prove existence of minimizers in restricted ranges; general degree existence is left open.
status_evidence.claim: Existence is known only under conditions ensuring no energy splitting, not for all integer degrees.

status_evidence.title: Existence Theory Based on the Minimization of the Energy (Skyrme model chapter)
status_evidence.snippet: Existence results for Skyrme's problem rely on strong density approximations, which remain a delicate open problem for general degrees.
status_evidence.claim: General-degree existence in the classical Skyrme model is not fully resolved.
